- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot true values, particularly after sharp upward spikes in history.
- Model underestimates late-period prices (last 5–10 days of 30d) — true values often rise above forecasted levels.
- Mean reversion is not captured: model fails to adjust downward after sustained high prices.
- Forecast lag: model reacts too slowly to recent price drops or corrections — underestimates downward momentum.
- Overshoot correction: if forecast exceeds true value by >5% in any day, reduce by 1–2% for next day’s forecast.
- Horizon bias: 30d forecasts should be calibrated to reflect recent trend persistence, not historical mean.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs — if last 5 days are rising, don’t assume continuation beyond 30d.
- Use moving average of last 7–10 days as a baseline to anchor forecast, especially when true values deviate from model.
